scope: Correct independent current-day Usage oracle timestamp precision; preserve strict equality and production rollup semantics.

source.state: uncommitted incremental shared worktree; not final acceptance
source.note: Concurrent unrelated source changes were present; archive-time source hashes do not claim final-source capacity acceptance. release-enabled-scale.mjs fixture setup is separately maintained.

finding.before: PostgreSQL observation timestamps retain microseconds; pg Date conversion truncated these to milliseconds before the old oracle used floating-point sums and Math.round. An observation 0.499999 seconds before cutoff wrongly became 0.500 seconds and rounded from0 to1.
finding.after: All raw-query callers select exact integer epoch microseconds as text. BigInt independently deduplicates by second, caps attribution at15seconds and cutoff, sums exactly, and rounds nonnegative half-up once per student for this fixed one-grain current-day fixture.

commands.red: node --test --test-name-pattern="preserves microseconds below a half-second" scripts/load/usage/local-usage-scale.test.mjs (new regression, before oracle correction)

diagnostics: Fixed-size counts only: microsecond precision, included/deduplicated observations, submillisecond count, exact versus legacy rounded totals and number of rounding-sensitive students. No raw observation times, identifiers, URLs or user content.
limitations: The original failing current-day raw observations were not retained before owned fixture cleanup. This synthetic proof confirms an oracle defect, not that the original aggregate was correct. A fresh corrected run must prove equality.

The current-day oracle assumes one class/session/domain/classification grain per student; known ixl.com educational classification and fixed current sessions support that fixture assumption. It is not a general multi-grain oracle.
No tolerance, timeout, infrastructure or production rollup semantics changed. This archive establishes neither capacity nor deployment readiness.
Native proof uses only local PostgreSQL numeric expressions over synthetic VALUES, not restricted-role application/RLS coverage.
sanitation: User home paths, connection URLs and JWT-shaped values redacted; original and sanitized hashes retained.
